published_statement: VERDICT (Sec. II.C, p.9), in full: 'Short wormholes, those allowing for causality violations, can only be constructed and sustained when the achronal ANEC is violated [10]. As we showed, the self-consistent, effective, ANEC is only violated when we have large field values, an unphysical effect if we view non-minimal coupling as an EFT. Long wormholes such as the one in Ref. [13] do not require the violation of the achronal ANEC as there are no achronal null geodesics passing through their throat. While there is no relevant theorem, it is obvious that the violation of effective ANEC is needed to sustain long wormholes. Considering only cases where the connected areas are asymptotically flat, the divergence of null geodesics passing through the throat requires the violation of average null convergence condition and thus the effective ANEC. This point requires further consideration, but so far it seems that it is impossible to construct traversable wormholes in the Jordan frame without unphysical field values. In that sense the two frames can be considered equivalent.' CLASSICAL (Sec. II.B, eqs. 19-20, p.7): effective ANEC integral = INT dlambda [1 - 8 pi xi G_N (1-4xi) phi^2]/(1 - 8 pi G_N xi phi^2)^2 (dphi/dlambda)^2 'where we discarded the boundary terms, assuming a smooth geodesic. Then it is obvious that the effective ANEC integrand is non-negative for xi < 0 and xi > 1/4. For 0 < xi < 1/4 it is positive for small field values, 8 pi xi(1-4xi) G_N phi^2 < 1, and negative for large values.' SEMICLASSICAL (Sec. IV.C, eq. 89, p.21): 'INT dx^- <T_--(x^+ = beta, x^-, y = 0)>_psi >= 0. We see that, as in the classical case discussed in Sec. II B we recover ANEC for any coupling in Minkowski spacetime. In the classical case we can do that, for bounded field values, for any spacetime curvature using the effective null energy.' ABSTRACT: 'Under this assumption [NMC as an EFT in which the field value is controlled by the cutoff], the average null energy condition, whose violation is necessary to allow traversable wormholes, is obeyed both classically and in the context of quantum field theory.' DISCUSSION (p.28): 'traversable wormholes are only possible if the effective average null energy condition (ANEC) is violated. Classically the violation of the effective ANEC is restricted to large field values, while semiclassically, the smeared null energy admits a lower bound dependent on the cutoff. Bounded field values additionally lead to a semiclassical proof of ANEC.'
published_hypotheses: H1 EFT assumption, ADOPTED not derived (abstract 'we adopt the view'; Sec. I eq. 2): NMC is the first term of an EFT with a single cutoff, k^2_max ~ phi_max^{4/(n-2)} ~ M^2_cutoff; 'unphysical' means outside this EFT. Sec. V motivates it (tower of irrelevant operators in the Einstein frame; loss of semiclassical path-integral control in the Jordan frame), which the tree reports (candidates.py:215-220).

H2 classical effective ANEC: effective stress tensor T_eff of eq. (15) (curvature terms moved to the geometry side), integral over an ENTIRE null geodesic, boundary terms discarded ('assuming a smooth geodesic'; for the plain ANEC eq. 17 'assuming that the field has asymptotically vanishing derivatives'); any curvature.

H3 field bound as it enters the classical result: needed ONLY for 0 < xi < 1/4, and there it is 8 pi xi (1-4xi) G_N phi^2 < 1 (weaker than the EFT bound 8 pi G xi phi^2 < 1); for xi < 0 and xi > 1/4 the integrand is non-negative at all field values (away from the pole 8 pi G xi phi^2 = 1).

H4 semiclassical ANEC (eq. 89): free scalar (massive or massless, eq. 7 with V = m^2 phi^2/2), n-dimensional MINKOWSKI spacetime, Hadamard states in the class <:phi^2:>_psi <= phi^2_max (eq. 79) with phi_max finite, smearing limit delta+ -> 0, delta- -> inf, delta+ delta- fixed, with (1/delta+)F^2 -> A delta(x+ - beta) (eq. 88); the quantity bounded is <T_--> (ordinary), not an effective stress tensor.
H5 in curved spacetime the semiclassical result is only the state-dependent smeared bound, Thm IV.1 eq. (72) (Hadamard states, smooth sampling), not an ANEC.

H6 the ANEC-violation requirement: a theorem only for SHORT (causality-violating) wormholes, via achronal ANEC (Graham & Olum, ref. [10]); for LONG wormholes 'there is no relevant theorem', argued for 'cases where the connected areas are asymptotically flat', and 'This point requires further consideration'.
H7 Jordan frame, single real scalar, classical Einstein equation G = 8 pi G_N T_eff (eq. 14).
hypothesis_drift: HEDGE DROPPED -- candidates.py:227-229 (repeated index3.py:1185, paper/CLAIMS.md:2259-2260) quote the verdict's tail 'it seems that it is impossible ...' as 'THEIR OWN VERDICT', 'quoted rather than paraphrased'. The words are verbatim (checked against src/2309.10848.flat), but the sentence's head 'This point requires further consideration, but so far' is cut, and the two preceding sentences that scope it ('While there is no relevant theorem, it is obvious ...'; 'Considering only cases where the connected areas are asymptotically flat') are not carried. The canonical entry's kind 'theorem' (canonical.json) is stronger than the source, which states there is no theorem for long wormholes. (The tree itself keeps 'it seems' and attaches no status word; the over-reach is in the silence about the scope, not in a misquotation.)

REQUIREMENT WIDENED -- candidates.py:230 and CLAIMS.md:2261 'the effective ANEC -- the thing that must be violated'. Source: a theorem (achronal ANEC, ref. [10]) only for short/causality-violating wormholes; for long wormholes an argument restricted to asymptotically flat connected regions, flagged 'requires further consideration'. The tree's unqualified 'must' follows the source's own unhedged Abstract/Discussion wording ('whose violation is necessary', 'only possible if'), so the widening is partly the source's internal inconsistency, recorded as such.

QUANTITY AND BACKGROUND DRIFT (semiclassical) -- candidates.py:230-231 and index3.py:1185 'the effective ANEC ... IS OBEYED both classically and semiclassically once field values are bounded'. Source: the semiclassical result (eq. 89) is the ORDINARY ANEC for <T_--> in MINKOWSKI spacetime (free scalar, <:phi^2:> <= phi^2_max); the effective ANEC is established only classically (eq. 20); in curved spacetime the semiclassical statement is the state-dependent smeared bound (72), and the Discussion says 'Bounded field values additionally lead to a semiclassical proof of ANEC' -- ANEC, not effective ANEC. CLAIMS.md:2261-2262 drops 'semiclassically' and so does not carry this drift.

COMPLETE-GEODESIC HYPOTHESIS DROPPED -- candidates.py:229-231, CLAIMS.md:2261: 'obeyed once field values are bounded' names only the field bound. The source's integral is over an entire geodesic with boundary terms discarded; rederive C3 shows the (19) integral is NEGATIVE (-0.1237) on a finite segment around a local minimum of phi^2 with a phi^2 <= 0.30 at xi = 1/6 -- the effective NEC is violated pointwise at small field values (source eq. 18), so the averaging hypothesis is load-bearing.

FIELD-BOUND FORM (not a drift against the tree, recorded for accuracy) -- the tree's bound phi^2_max <~ (8 pi G_N |xi|)^-1 (candidates.py:219) is the EFT (Sec. V) bound; the classical effective-ANEC result needs less: nothing for xi < 0 or xi > 1/4, and 8 pi xi(1-4xi) G phi^2 < 1 for 0 < xi < 1/4 (z3 B1-B3). At conformal coupling violation needs 8 pi G xi phi^2 > 3 (z3 B6). The tree's use is therefore conservative on this point.

'UNPHYSICAL' RESTS ON AN ADOPTED EFT VIEW -- candidates.py:215-220 reports the Sec. V motivation correctly ('The cutoff that would work is the one the EFT excludes'); the drift is only that the verdict is presented as the authors' finding rather than as conditional on H1, which the source adopts ('we adopt the view', abstract).

rederivation.outcome: REDERIVE PASS, 16/16 (output saved to rederive/2309.10848-verdict-anec.out). A1 (sympy, arbitrary phi(lambda)): (19) - (20) integrand = d/dlambda[-xi (phi^2)'/(1 - a phi^2)] exactly, so (20) equals (19) exactly when boundary terms vanish; A2 numerator = 1 - 8 pi G xi (1-4xi) phi^2 as printed; A3 numerator -> 4 xi > 0 at the pole. z3 (each with vacuity guard): B1 xi<0 => positive at all field values; B2 xi>1/4 => positive at all field values; B3 0<xi<1/4 with the EFT bound 8 pi G xi phi^2 < 1 => positive; B4 negativity requires 8 pi G xi phi^2 > 1/(1-4xi) > 1; B5 sat witness xi = 1/8, x = 17 (non-vacuous); B6 at xi = 1/6 negativity impossible for 8 pi G xi phi^2 <= 3. Numeric: C1/C2 complete geodesic, Gaussian profile inside the bound (peak a phi^2 = 0.81), xi = 1/6: (19) = (20) = 2.58031601 > 0; C3 finite segment: -0.123712 < 0. Semiclassical limit (sympy): D1 first term of (85) after ANEC normalisation = N_n delta+/(A alpha^n) (source: 'delta+/(A alpha^n)', agrees); D2 second term with phi_max fixed = C|xi|phi^2_max delta+/(A alpha^2) -> 0; D3 with phi~_max fixed = ... delta+/(A alpha^n), which is the source's printed 'delta+/(A alpha^4)' at n = 4 -- the printed exponent matches only that reading in n = 4 (a reading ambiguity in a general-n section, not an error; both readings -> 0); D4 guard: with no field bound (phi^2_max ~ delta-^2) the second term diverges, so the finite phi_max hypothesis is load-bearing. Verdict sentence itself: nothing to re-derive -- the source offers it as an argument ('no relevant theorem'), so it is checked as a READ, not re-derived.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the authors had in 2023: the free-field Hadamard QEI machinery (their Thm IV.1), the DSNEC (ref. [14]), Barcelo-Visser's classical case analysis (ref. [2]), Graham-Olum's achronal-ANEC theorem (ref. [10]) and the Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov long wormhole (ref. [13]). EVIDENCE THAT NO DATUM IS MISSING: the classical half is a sign identity -- re-derived exactly here (A1-A3, z3 B1-B6) -- and contains no measured quantity; the semiclassical half is a limit that holds for every finite phi_max (D1-D2). G_N enters only as the scale of the bound, and xi (unmeasured for a generic scalar; for the Higgs only |xi| < 2.6e15, Atkins-Calmet, READ in stage gr-qc_0003025-anec-cases) is carried as a parameter, so no measurement could move the sign. EVIDENCE FOR M's DIRECTION (incompleteness, not wrongness): what the authors lacked was not data but theorems -- they say so ('there is no relevant theorem' for long wormholes; 'This point requires further consideration'), they had no semiclassical effective-ANEC in curved spacetime (only the state-dependent smeared bound (72)), and no state-independent QEI for the interacting Einstein-frame theory ('no known state-independent bounds in n > 2'). Those are named gaps in the source's own text, so the verdict is incomplete where the tree reads it as settled. Whether a later theorem closes the long-wormhole gap (topological censorship via the ANCC identity; Kontou et al. 2405.05963) is not established here -- both NAMED-NOT-READ. EFFECT ON THE TREE'S CONCLUSION: none in either direction. candidates CANDIDATES['non-minimal coupling'] fails on the tree's separate magnitude gate (closes only at l_UV = 3.159514 l_P, audited under key 2309.10848), which does not rest on the verdict sentence; narrowing the verdict does not rescue the candidate, and filling the gap would not strengthen the magnitude result.
grade_evidence: The source is READ (v1 full text, cached alphaXiv extraction, quotations checked in this stage). The quotation in candidates.py:227-229 / :408-409 is VERBATIM. The mathematics under it re-derives: effective ANEC eq. (20) from (19) is an exact identity up to a total derivative (sympy A1), its sign regions are z3-valid with vacuity guards (B1-B6; the EFT bound implies non-negativity for every xi, and at xi = 1/6 violation needs 8 pi G xi phi^2 > 3), and the semiclassical limit (85) -> (89) goes to zero for every finite phi_max (D1-D2) and fails without a bound (D4). No datum enters, so none can move it. But the tree's use is broader than the source on a smaller class in three named ways: (i) the verdict is quoted without its head 'This point requires further consideration, but so far' and without its scope -- a theorem (achronal ANEC, ref. [10]) only for short/causality-violating wormholes, and for long wormholes 'no relevant theorem', asymptotically flat connected regions only -- so 'the thing that must be violated' (candidates.py:230) and the canonical kind 'theorem' over-state it; (ii) 'the effective ANEC IS OBEYED ... semiclassically' (candidates.py:230-231, index3.py:1185) -- the source's semiclassical result is the ordinary ANEC for <T_--> in Minkowski spacetime for a free scalar with <:phi^2:> <= phi^2_max; the effective ANEC is proved only classically; (iii) 'once field values are bounded' drops the complete-geodesic/boundary-term hypothesis, shown load-bearing (C3: -0.1237 on a finite segment at small field). Not WRONG: no counterexample to any FFKP statement was found or built, and the source's own wording is inconsistent (the unhedged Abstract/Discussion vs the hedged Sec. II.C), so the tree followed a sentence the authors wrote. Not over-represented against the source either: the field-bound hypothesis the tree uses is STRONGER than the classical result needs (B1-B3), and the downstream verdict (NMC candidate fails) does not rest on this sentence. The D3 exponent ('alpha^4' printed where general n gives alpha^n with phi~ fixed, alpha^2 with phi_max fixed) is a reading ambiguity, recorded, not quoted as an error.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree carrying the source's scope -- 'short (causality-violating) wormholes: theorem; long wormholes: argued, asymptotically flat, no theorem' -- and 'semiclassically: ANEC in Minkowski for bounded <:phi^2:>' in place of 'effective ANEC semiclassically'; or a READ theorem closing the long-wormhole gap (e.g. topological censorship applied through the ANCC = effective-ANEC identity, or Kontou et al. 2405.05963) plus a curved-space semiclassical effective ANEC. The SciPost version (Phys. 16, 119 (2024)) could also change the grade if its wording differs from v1 -- it has not been read. To WRONG: a smooth, asymptotically flat traversable wormhole in the Jordan frame with 8 pi G xi phi^2 < 1 everywhere, sourced by a NMC scalar -- none is known here and none was constructed. To OPEN: loss of the cached v1 text without a re-read.
